From the table of Laplace transforms, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{\operatorname{cos}⁡2t} & =\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+{2}^{2}}=\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+4},\,s>0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by applying the inverse Laplace transform to the above result, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{\operatorname{cos}⁡2t} & =\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+4} \\ {L}^{-1}{L{\operatorname{cos}⁡2t}} & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+4}} \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡2t & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+4}} \\ {L}^{-1}{\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+4}} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡2t.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the multiplicative property of the inverse Laplace transform, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}\cdot {L}^{-1}{\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+4}}=\frac{3}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡2t \\ {L}^{-1}{\frac{3s}{4{s}^{2}+16}}=\frac{3}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡2t.\end{aligned}
$$
